summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Borealis through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Key discussion points: how per-route dashboards map to their API routes, breakdown of token cost vs infra, routing/fallbacks between hosted and dedicated, caching and batching impact on unit economics, and enterprise security requirements. Customer asked about data residency, SSO, and audit logs. Agreed to provide security docs, per-route cost spreadsheet, and run a dedicated capacity sizing session.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-29 15:30 PST | Duration: ~45 min | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sophie (Borealis Head of AI), Marcus (Platform Eng), Dana (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya Singh: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Liam, wanna quick intro?
[00:06] Liam Chen: Yep, Liam Chen, systems engineer, I'll run the demo and jump into the cost calc and sizing later.
[00:12] Sophie Alvarez: Hi, Sophie here, Head of AI at Borealis. Marcus and Dana are with me.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Marcus, platform eng. We'll be looking mainly at per-route cost and how inference fits into our peak weekends.
[00:25] Dana Ortiz: Dana, procurement, hi all.
[00:28] Maya Singh: Great, quick agenda — run console, look at usage analytics, deep dive per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, Q&A, next steps.
[00:38] Liam Chen: So opening the console — first thing you'll see is the usage map, token distribution by model and route, and latency percentiles. Note these colors are configurable.
[00:48] Sophie Alvarez: Do you pull logs from our VPC, or is this in Redwood hosted?
[00:52] Liam Chen: For hosted we ingest metrics, but for private/dedicated we can ship metrics to your monitoring stack. We keep the tokenized counts, not raw payloads by default, unless you enable full payload logging.
[01:05] Sophie Alvarez: Ok that sounds good. Also curious about how to attribute cost per product route — we have a commerce checkout route and a search route that are heavy.
[01:15] Liam Chen: That's where per-route dashboards come in — you can attach route tags in the SDK or via gateway rules. The console shows tokens, calls, avg latency, and cost estimate per route. Here's an example view for a customer — you can see checkout has high token volume but lower latency than chat.
[01:35] Marcus Lee: How precise is the cost estimate? We need to reconcile with our internal billing.
[01:40] Liam Chen: We surface token cost and infra allocation. For hosted it's a straightforward per-token plus model premium. For dedicated we show a blended infra cost based on reserved capacity and observed utilization; we estimate unit cost using a model of bins — it's an estimate but usually within 8-12% of actual until you run longer runs.
[02:00] Sophie Alvarez: What about batching and KV cache effects? Checkout is very prefixy.
[02:05] Liam Chen: Batching and KV caching can cut tokens and GPU time substantially. The console also has a heatmap showing cache hit rates and batching efficiency per route. Note some transcriptions in logs might show KV "cash" — small bugs in auto labeling sometimes.
[02:20] Maya Singh: We also show suggested optimizations per route in the Console's Optimize tab: quantization suggestions, batch window tweaks, and cache TTLs.
[02:32] Marcus Lee: For dedicated vs hosted — if we go dedicated, do we lose access to new model variants?
[02:38] Liam Chen: You can pin versions, but you also get access to the model catalog. In some cases, very new model binaries roll out to hosted first; dedicated fleets get them on the normal cadence. We can prioritize critical patches for enterprise customers.
[02:52] Sophie Alvarez: Security — SSO, SAML, KMS integration? We need SOC 2 and audit logs for PCI scope.
[02:59] Maya Singh: Yes, we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and integration with customer KMS/HSM in Private. We provide detailed audit logs and can ship logs to your SIEM. SOC 2 attestation is available; we'll send the packet.
[03:15] Dana Ortiz: Any data residency guarantees e.g., EU-only?
[03:18] Liam Chen: For hosted we have region selection; for Private you can fully control routing and data residency. Dedicated can be regional as well.
[03:27] Sophie Alvarez: Great. On the cost breakdown slide, can you walk through an example of a per-route computation?
[03:33] Liam Chen: Sure — take checkout: median prompt tokens 70, response tokens 120, avg latency 180 ms. Token cost X per 1k tokens, plus infra amortized per query. Console shows tokens consumed, estimated token charge, and infra per-query by dividing reserved infra cost by observed qps for the period.
[03:53] Marcus Lee: So if we have spiky traffic on Black Friday, how does autoscaling and burst capacity work with dedicated?
[03:58] Liam Chen: Dedicated supports configured autoscale and burst pools. You can set a burst budget per month; the console simulates costs of different burst budgets. For hard spikes, we have smart routing to fallback to hosted or lower-precision quantized variants to preserve latency SLOs.
[04:18] Sophie Alvarez: Any example of the cost delta when using 4-bit quantization?
[04:22] Liam Chen: We have a chart — quantization reduced infra unit cost by roughly 30-45% for our sample workload, but quality tradeoffs depend on task and prompt. Optimize suggests candidate routes for quantization.
[04:38] Maya Singh: Quick note — we often recommend running a short A/B on 2-3 critical prompts to check quality before rolling quantized models for a route.
[04:50] Marcus Lee: Can we export per-route billing CSV?
[04:54] Liam Chen: Yes, export to CSV or link to your billing S3. You can also set per-route budgets and alerts.
[05:05] Sophie Alvarez: On integration — our gateway tags routes at the edge with X-Route header, will that work?
[05:10] Liam Chen: Absolutely. Any header-based tagging works, and you can also instrument SDK to set operation=checkout etc.
[05:18] Dana Ortiz: From procurement perspective — what's the pricing model for reserved capacity vs hosted?
[05:23] Maya Singh: Hosted is usage-based per token + per-feature premium. Dedicated is reserved monthly commit that yields better unit prices plus burst options. We'll share a model spreadsheet tailored to your traffic mix.
[05:36] Sophie Alvarez: We have concerns about observability retention — how long are logs kept?
[05:40] Liam Chen: Default is 30 days for detailed traces, longer aggregated metrics retained 13 months; retention options available as add-ons.
[05:50] Marcus Lee: Anything else on audit and compliance?
[05:52] Maya Singh: We can do SOC 2, ISO docs, contract language for audit, and we support customer-managed KMS for Private.
[06:02] Liam Chen: Jumping back to the console, here's a per-route tag filter — I'll filter to 'checkout' and show 7-day rollup. You can see cache hit improves cost 22% last week after we enabled prefix caching.
[06:20] Sophie Alvarez: Nice, can we get that same heatmap for our test data?
[06:23] Liam Chen: Yes, if you share sample logs we can prototype; Marcus, we'll need your anonymized request/response shapes and route mapping.
[06:33] Marcus Lee: I'll extract a 7-day sample without PII.
[06:36] Dana Ortiz: Timeline — we're aiming for pilot in January, decision by end of Q1.
[06:42] Maya Singh: Sounds good. Next steps we'll send security packet, pricing, and set up dedicated sizing call.
[06:49] Sophie Alvarez: Can Liam also run a rough perf estimate for our projected 2k qps?
[06:54] Liam Chen: Yes, I can do an estimate and a couple sizing configs.
[06:58] Maya Singh: Okay, wrapping up — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and scheduling notes.
[07:05] (call continues with deeper technical Q&A and a 30-minute sizing + billing reconciliation session covering: model catalog variants, rollout policies, quantization A/B plan, retention and audit exports, SSO setup, KMS key exchange process, and an example per-route CSV walk-through).
[37:10] Liam Chen: Quick notes from sizing — for 2k qps with 70/120 token profile and 95th latency target 250ms, two config options: 1) Dedicated with 8x A100 equiv, 2) Hosted + burst with smart routing. Will send spreadsheet.
[40:45] Sophie Alvarez: That's helpful, appreciate the options.
[41:00] Maya Singh: Final recap — action items and deliverables, we'll email materials tomorrow and schedule the sizing deep-dive for next Tuesday.
[41:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: informal, occasionally mis-attributed speaker labels and a few words transcribed incorrectly (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash), timestamps approximate.
